title: LD_SO_CACHE and fragmented VRAM debug log
content:
Quick brain dump — trying to capture commands I ran, outputs I saw, and ideas to try next. This is messy; notes to future-me and anyone else who ends up chasing these OOMs.

Summary of incident:
- Node: rwd-infer-gpu-12 (p4d-sim, local staging)
- Symptom: repeated CUDA OOM during warmup of transformer model at batch_size=4, seq_len=2048. Failures inconsistent across restarts.
- Likely contributors: mixed libcuda / driver version mismatch after recent package bump; ld.so cache pointing to old libcuda; nvlink/peer access flapping; large kvcache fragmentation.

Commands / outputs I collected (chronological):
1) docker run (how model starts in prod):
   docker run --gpus all --shm-size=1g --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID rwd-infer:staging-20260221 /bin/bash -lc "python serve.py --model my-transformer --batch 4"

2) nvidia-smi (immediately after failure):
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   | NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12 Driver Version: 525.85.12 CUDA Version: 12.1           |
   | GPU 0: Tesla V100-SXM2 (UUID: GPU-xxxx)  32GiB                             |
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   | Processes:                                                                  |
   |   12345 python3   C   8007MiB                                                  |
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   Observed: process shows ~8GB reserved, but ML process crashed with CUDA OOM for 12GB allocation. Suggests fragmentation / allocation failure rather than total memory exhausted.

3) dmesg snippets: (when OOM triggered)
   [ 2314.727643] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e.0): 13, pid=12345 0 00000000 00000000
   [ 2314.727645] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
   Note: "fallen off the bus" correlates with a driver fault but later recovered — process crashes instead of system panic.

4) ldconfig / ldd checks I ran:
   # on host
   $ ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
   libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1

   # inside container (same image, mounted nvidia libs)
   $ ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda
   libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f9b...)

   Observed mismatch: host points to system path, container points to mounted nvidia lib at /usr/local/nvidia/lib64. After recent driver update we have both 525.xx and a leftover 515.* copy in the image overlay — hypothesis: stale symlink or LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering causes a mixture of driver / runtime symbols.

5) python trace (torch) at oom moment:
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 12.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 8.12 GiB already allocated; 3.25 GiB free; 20.62 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
   Notes: The numbers look inconsistent with nvidia-smi: "3.25 GiB free" vs nvidia-smi showing much more free space. This often happens when fragmentation and reserved caching differ across cudaMalloc calls.

6) the container env vars I checked:
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
   LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/nvidia/lib64:/usr/local/nvidia/lib:/opt/conda/lib
   NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility,graphics

   I suspect LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering is fine but the overlay /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 contains both a stub and the updated libcuda depending on host runtime.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Mixed driver/runtime libs (libcuda) in mount vs host lead to subtle symbol/version mismatch causing memory allocation issues and NVRM Xid. Evidence: ldconfig vs ldd mismatch, leftover 515.* files in /opt/images/driver-archive.
- H2: KV cache fragmentation in our runtime paired with prealloc/reserve settings causing fragmentation; model warmup pattern triggers many small ephemeral allocations that leave non-coalesced holes. Evidence: PyTorch reserved vs allocated mismatch, inconsistent free numbers.
- H3: NVLink or Peer access instability (PCI errors) leads to repeated device resets; process then fails allocation. Evidence: "GPU has fallen off the bus" in dmesg, occasionally shows PCIe error counters in ethtool-like logs.
- H4: Docker runtime GPU isolation bug when using --shm-size low; some libraries try to mlock and fail causing driver to misbehave. Less likely but quick to test by bumping shm-size.

Commands / experiments to run (next):
- Reproduce minimal: start Python REPL with torch.cuda and run allocation loop to reproduce exact allocation size that crashes. Script: reproduce_oom.py (below).
- Run container with --pid=host and strace the python to catch last syscalls before NVRM Xid.
- Swap to host-mounted driver directory only (unmount /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 inside container) and run again to force host driver libs.
- Build small C program that calls cuInit, cuDeviceGet, cudaMalloc repeatedly to see if CUDA runtime or driver triggers Xid outside of torch.
- Temporarily set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to reduce fragmentation and see if crash disappears. Set PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 as alternative to test caching effects.
- Increase --shm-size to 4g and re-run to see if behavior changes.

Quick reproduce script (notes):
-------------------------------
# reproduce_oom.py (local quick test)
import torch
import time

torch.cuda.init()
print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))
try:
    for i in range(100):
        print('alloc iter', i)
        a = torch.empty((1024,1024,512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)  # ~1GB each
        time.sleep(0.2)
except Exception as e:
    print('failed', e)
    import traceback; traceback.print_exc()
-------------------------------
Notes: reduce size / stride to tune to where OOM appears reliably.

Observed anomalies worth tracking:
- Sometimes a kernel update on the host triggers a short window where libcuda in the image points to a removed inode (file replaced), containers keep old handle which is stale — need to check inode numbers.
- When the node is rebooted, problem often temporarily disappears (consistent with stale module handles).
- On one run, I saw libcudart.so.11.0 and libcudart.so.12 both present in LD path; ldd showed symbol resolution to 11.0 but driver is 525 which expects some 12.x symbols — potential ABI mismatch.

Notes-to-self about debug instrumentation:
- Add early logging in our runtime that prints: CUDA driver version (cuDriverGetVersion), cudaRuntimeGetVersion, and dlopen/dladdr resolution of libcuda path before model load.
- Emit the process' heap maps (/proc/<pid>/maps) at OOM time (if possible) so we can correlate address ranges to loaded libs.
- In CI, add a cheap allocation test after container start that checks cudaMalloc(1) and logs driver/runtime versions; fail fast if mismatch detected.

Relevant snippets I saved to /tmp/oom-dumps/ (on node):
- /tmp/oom-dumps/20260301-1234-nvidia-smi.txt
- /tmp/oom-dumps/20260301-dmesg.txt
- /tmp/oom-dumps/20260301-ldconfig.txt
- /tmp/oom-dumps/reproduce_oom_trace.log

Slack notes to post once we have repro:
- Summarize with exact driver/runtime versions, Docker image tag, what changed recently (image bump on 2026-02-20), and a minimal repro script. Ask infra to check if driver rollout hit this host last week. Link GH issue and attach logs.

Possible remediations (temporary):
- Force consistent lib path: mount host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu into container at /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 (ugly but forces host libs).
- Set PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 in staging to see if fragmentation is main culprit.
- Add startup test to fail fast and avoid serving if driver/runtime mismatch detected.

Longer-term:
- Work with infra to create a small driver compatibility test harness that runs as DaemonSet/agent and reports nodes with mixed lib versions or leftover driver stashes.
- Consider runtime change: prefer cudaMallocAsync where available to reduce fragmentation and improve release semantics (needs CUDA 11.8+ / driver support).

Random notes / TODOs:
- Check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log for recent driver installs (timestamps).
- Run "stat /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1" on host and in container and compare inodes.
- Check whether nvidia-container-runtime-hook is up-to-date in our base image.

If anyone else picks this up, start with the reproduce_oom.py snippet and try toggling PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING and TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF. Then try forcing host libcuda into the container to see if OOM/Xid still occurs.

End of notes.
